title: Watching your savings grow with interest
examples: How long does it take money to double?

explain.say: Imagine planting a mango seed that grows a tree, which drops seeds that grow more trees. Money can grow like that! Look at the board: a curve that starts slowly and then shoots up. That is your savings growing with interest.

draw.text: Watching your savings grow with interest

explain.say: Let's start small. Put 100 in a savings account paying 10 percent a year; we use 10 to keep the maths easy. Interest is extra money the bank pays you for keeping your money there. Look at the blocks: 100 plus 10 makes 110 after one year.

Now the magic. In year two you earn 10 percent of 110, not just of 100. See the blocks: 110 plus 11 makes 121. Earning interest on your interest is called compound interest. Can you spot the extra 1? It grew from last year's interest!

Back to the curve. Keep going, and by year 10 your 100 has become about 259. See the mark? The curve gets steeper because each year the pile earning interest is bigger. What do you think happens by year 20?

By year 20 it is about 673, nearly seven times what you put in, without adding a coin! Fantastic! Here is a trick: divide 72 by the interest rate to guess how many years money takes to double. At 10 percent, about 7 years.

faq.a: Interest is extra money paid for using money. A bank pays you interest on savings, and you pay interest when you borrow.
asks: Why does the bank pay me?

faq.a: Compound interest means you earn interest on your interest as well as on the money you first saved, so the total grows faster and faster.
It is a quick way to estimate doubling time: divide 72 by the yearly interest rate. At 6 percent, money doubles in about 12 years; at 10 percent, in about 7.
asks: How long does money take to double?

faq.q: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
faq.a: Simple interest is paid only on the money you first put in. Compound interest is paid on the growing total, including past interest. After two years at 10 percent, 100 becomes 120 with simple interest but 121 with compound.
asks: Simple or compound, which is better?

faq.q: Does borrowing work the same way?
faq.a: Yes, and that is the danger. Unpaid debt on credit cards or loans also compounds, so it can grow quickly if you only pay a little back.

facts: 100 at 10% compound interest grows to about 259 after 10 years and about 673 after 20 years.
The rule of 72 estimates doubling time as 72 divided by the yearly percentage rate.

quiz.say: You save 100 at 10% interest for one year. How much do you have?
quiz.show: You save 100 at 10% interest for one year. How much do you have?
quiz.why: 10 percent of 100 is 10, so you have 110.

wrong.0: That forgets the interest you earned.
wrong.2: That would be 100 percent interest, not 10.

quiz.say: At 10% compound interest, what does 110 become after another year?
quiz.show: At 10% compound interest, what does 110 become after another year?
quiz.why: 10 percent of 110 is 11, and 110 plus 11 is 121.

wrong.0: 120 is simple interest, paid only on the first 100.
wrong.1: That adds just 1; the interest is 10 percent of 110.
